Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)


Reconstruct from the supplied RGB only. Use the fixed SceneAct API and meaningful
multipart Asset groups. No tools, file exploration, reference textures, projections,
additional views, rendering calls or saving calls. The runner renders and saves.
Do not change runner settings, resolution, sampling, backend or resource limits.

Before coding, state a compact visible-image specification: major silhouettes and
normalized bounds (top-left origin), architectural boundary endpoints, perspective
line directions, foreground cropping, and occlusion order. Distinguish observations
from uncertain depth assumptions. Name camera position, target, lens and major object
dimensions as parameters. Build all substantial visible objects on the first attempt.
Match the visible negative spaces as carefully as occupied regions: openings between
supports, under furniture, around foreground objects and through the room.

Keep construction economical. SceneAct sweep_tube emits a sphere at every point and
one cylinder per segment; fillet_box emits many separate meshes. Long decorative
loops and floor grids can create thousands of objects before rendering even begins.
Use boxes for flat parts, rods for straight parts, and short sweeps for curved outlines.
Restrict repeated geometry to visible regions. Use procedural material patterns for
fine surface markings, never the input image. Avoid modeling subpixel stitches, grain,
weave and hidden flooring as separate objects. Preserve object identities and editable
parts; do not merge the entire scene. Prefer a few hundred primitives where possible,
without omitting important objects. Simplify detail further when time is short.

Check source before returning every program:
- fillet_box requires 0 < radius <= half the smallest size component.
- rod endpoints are keyword arguments and must be distinct. Consecutive sweep points
  must be distinct. All dimensions must be positive and finite.
- include replaces a child with the same key; include every loop index in repeated keys.
- Transform pivots default to bounding-box centers; specify other pivots explicitly.
- realize clears Blender. Create camera, lights and material customization afterward.
  Obtain bpy.context.scene after realize. Create its world if None and enable use_nodes
  before accessing Background. Mesh names need not equal SceneAct include keys:
  target mesh descendants of the relevant marker and copy shared materials for local edits.
- Keep all visible parts of an object under its meaningful assembly through revisions.

After rendering, compare actual images, not the intended effect of code. Use a small
residual table: region or landmark, reference estimate, rendered estimate, discrepancy,
likely cause, and proposed parameter change. Estimates are visual, not measurements.
Check architecture and foreground together before changing the camera. Global position
errors suggest aim/shift; slopes suggest orientation; near/far ratios suggest camera
position and lens. Local errors suggest geometry or placement. Explain any coupled
camera and geometry change. Prioritize silhouette, occlusion, framing, large color
regions and illumination over ornament. Avoid simultaneously darkening every material
and reducing all lights: isolate the dominant cause of a brightness discrepancy.
Do not infer hidden objects or exact physical dimensions from category conventions.

A visual audit is a model-only comparison, not permission to execute anything.
When requested, begin with BEST <step>, choosing the best available successful render
against the reference. This records a fallback, not a claim about an unrendered revision.
Then provide the requested critique and/or one complete standalone Python program in
one python fenced block. Preserve sound geometry and change at most three coherent
parameter families. Never return a patch. SELECT <step> ends reconstruction with that
successful output. DONE accepts the latest successful output. Missing or failed output
is a failure, not an image to critique. Repair the reported cause and related source
hazards; never invent metrics or claim visual validation of an unrendered program.

Observed image bounds use normalized coordinates with the origin at top left. The pale island occupies approximately `(0.33, 0.56)–(0.90, 0.85)`, with three broad drawer fronts and a visible left end. The suspended rectangular hood occupies `(0.42, 0.05)–(0.73, 0.44)`. A timber post fills `(0.17, 0.00)–(0.31, 0.99)`, obscuring the rear cabinetry. Dark cabinets, backsplash, an illuminated niche, and stacked ovens span the background. A small red kettle sits in the niche.

The floor meets the cabinetry along a boundary running approximately from `(0.00, 0.75)` through `(0.33, 0.69)` to `(1.00, 0.65)`. Ceiling beams descend diagonally toward the right; island depth edges rise toward the right. Vertical edges remain nearly vertical. The foreground post overlaps the cabinets and island’s left vicinity; the hood overlaps the backsplash and ovens. Open floor around the island and the dark gap beneath the hood are important negative spaces.

Depth assumptions: the island stands in front of a continuous rear kitchen wall; the timber posts support an exposed dark ceiling. Parameters below name the camera, island, hood, and room dimensions. Fine ornament is deferred.

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math

# Primary dimensions and camera parameters, in metres.
CAMERA_POSITION = (-3.65, -6.65, 1.95)
CAMERA_TARGET = (0.05, 0.65, 1.95)
CAMERA_LENS = 47
ROOM_WIDTH = 6.8
ROOM_DEPTH = 7.0
CEILING_HEIGHT = 3.75
ISLAND_WIDTH = 2.55
ISLAND_DEPTH = 1.08
ISLAND_HEIGHT = 0.99
HOOD_WIDTH = 1.10
HOOD_DEPTH = 0.87
HOOD_BOTTOM = 2.02
HOOD_TOP = 3.73

scene = Scene("Kitchen")

ivory = (.66, .67, .63)
counter = (.79, .80, .74)
black = (.035, .043, .042)
charcoal = (.065, .073, .070)
steel = (.36, .39, .38)
wood = (.39, .24, .125)
floor_color = (.60, .59, .54)

def add_box(asset, name, size, center, color):
    asset.include(name, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

architecture = Asset("Architecture")
add_box(architecture, "floor", (ROOM_WIDTH, ROOM_DEPTH, .12),
        (0, .2, -.06), floor_color)
add_box(architecture, "back_wall", (6.8, .16, 3.8),
        (0, 2.40, 1.9), (.26, .28, .26))
add_box(architecture, "left_wall", (.15, 5.6, 3.8),
        (-3.35, .2, 1.9), (.36, .37, .33))
add_box(architecture, "ceiling", (6.8, 7, .12),
        (0, .2, 3.81), (.045, .054, .051))

# Sparse floor joints, following large square tiles.
for i, x in enumerate([-3, -1.8, -.6, .6, 1.8, 3]):
    add_box(architecture, "floor_joint_x_%d" % i,
            (.008, 6.8, .002), (x, .2, .002), (.40, .41, .38))
for i, y in enumerate([-2.8, -1.6, -.4, .8, 2.0]):
    add_box(architecture, "floor_joint_y_%d" % i,
            (6.7, .008, .002), (0, y, .002), (.40, .41, .38))

# Exposed ceiling joists and two heavier longitudinal beams.
for i, y in enumerate([-1.6, -.75, .15, 1.05, 1.95]):
    add_box(architecture, "ceiling_joist_%d" % i,
            (6.5, .095, .20), (0, y, 3.63), (.035, .043, .041))
for i, x in enumerate([-.90, 1.55]):
    add_box(architecture, "main_ceiling_beam_%d" % i,
            (.25, 6.8, .32), (x, .2, 3.55), (.055, .066, .063))
scene.include("architecture", architecture)

posts = Asset("Timber supports")
add_box(posts, "foreground_post", (.38, .38, 3.8),
        (-1.72, -1.50, 1.90), wood)
add_box(posts, "far_right_post", (.19, .22, 3.65),
        (2.72, 2.00, 1.825), wood)
scene.include("posts", posts)

kitchen = Asset("Rear kitchen cabinetry")
# Left tall cupboard, largely hidden by the timber.
add_box(kitchen, "left_tall_carcass", (.92, .66, 2.30),
        (-2.13, 1.89, 1.15), black)
for i, z in enumerate([.58, 1.72]):
    add_box(kitchen, "left_tall_door_%d" % i, (.88, .035, 1.12),
            (-2.13, 1.54, z), charcoal)

# Base run and dark toe recess.
add_box(kitchen, "rear_toe", (3.45, .54, .13),
        (-.05, 1.91, .095), (.018, .022, .021))
add_box(kitchen, "rear_base", (3.5, .64, .78),
        (-.05, 1.90, .51), black)
add_box(kitchen, "rear_worktop", (3.56, .71, .045),
        (-.05, 1.86, .923), (.17, .18, .16))
for i, x in enumerate([-1.35, -.50, .35, 1.20]):
    add_box(kitchen, "rear_base_front_%d" % i,
            (.825, .025, .72), (x, 1.564, .53), charcoal)

# Upper black wall and shallow warm work niche.
add_box(kitchen, "backsplash", (3.45, .045, .75),
        (-.05, 2.238, 1.32), (.055, .063, .058))
add_box(kitchen, "upper_cabinet_run", (3.45, .43, .52),
        (-.05, 2.04, 1.99), black)
for i, x in enumerate([-1.34, -.48, .38, 1.24]):
    add_box(kitchen, "upper_front_%d" % i,
            (.84, .025, .49), (x, 1.812, 1.99), (.045, .052, .048))
add_box(kitchen, "niche_warm_back", (2.24, .025, .34),
        (-.54, 2.202, 1.12), (.31, .25, .21))
add_box(kitchen, "niche_light_strip", (2.24, .035, .016),
        (-.54, 1.829, 1.435), (.94, .80, .59))

# Right full-height cabinet bank and two built-in appliances.
add_box(kitchen, "right_tall_bank", (1.17, .76, 2.34),
        (1.90, 1.96, 1.17), black)
add_box(kitchen, "right_side_door", (.48, .035, 2.27),
        (2.23, 1.561, 1.17), charcoal)
add_box(kitchen, "oven_column_face", (.64, .035, 2.27),
        (1.64, 1.56, 1.17), (.07, .075, .069))
for i, z in enumerate([1.02, 1.51]):
    add_box(kitchen, "oven_frame_%d" % i, (.57, .05, .43),
            (1.64, 1.527, z), steel)
    add_box(kitchen, "oven_glass_%d" % i, (.48, .014, .29),
            (1.64, 1.495, z-.025), (.018, .034, .039))
    add_box(kitchen, "oven_control_%d" % i, (.49, .017, .055),
            (1.64, 1.480, z+.15), (.15, .17, .16))
    kitchen.include("oven_handle_%d" % i,
        rod(radius=.014, start=(1.42, 1.451, z+.095),
            end=(1.86, 1.451, z+.095), color=(.55, .57, .55)))
scene.include("rear_kitchen", kitchen)

island = Asset("Island with drawers and sink")
island_x = .15
island_y = -.05
add_box(island, "recessed_plinth", (2.40, .93, .10),
        (island_x, island_y+.025, .08), (.15, .17, .16))
add_box(island, "cabinet_body", (ISLAND_WIDTH, ISLAND_DEPTH, .83),
        (island_x, island_y, .545), ivory)
# Full uninterrupted left end panel.
add_box(island, "left_end_panel", (.035, 1.09, .88),
        (island_x-1.283, island_y, .55), (.59, .61, .58))
front_y = island_y - ISLAND_DEPTH/2 - .015
for i, z in enumerate([.275, .55, .825]):
    add_box(island, "drawer_%d" % i, (2.48, .028, .259),
            (island_x+.018, front_y, z), ivory)
    add_box(island, "drawer_reveal_%d" % i, (2.47, .015, .012),
            (island_x+.018, front_y-.006, z+.134),
            (.27, .29, .27))

# A slab assembled around an inset rectangular sink.
sink_x, sink_y = .60, .13
sink_w, sink_d = .60, .39
left_edge, right_edge = island_x-1.30, island_x+1.30
front_edge, back_edge = island_y-.565, island_y+.565
z_top = .985
add_box(island, "counter_left", (sink_x-sink_w/2-left_edge, 1.13, .045),
        ((left_edge+sink_x-sink_w/2)/2, island_y, z_top), counter)
add_box(island, "counter_right", (right_edge-sink_x-sink_w/2, 1.13, .045),
        ((right_edge+sink_x+sink_w/2)/2, island_y, z_top), counter)
add_box(island, "counter_front", (sink_w, sink_y-sink_d/2-front_edge, .045),
        (sink_x, (front_edge+sink_y-sink_d/2)/2, z_top), counter)
add_box(island, "counter_back", (sink_w, back_edge-sink_y-sink_d/2, .045),
        (sink_x, (back_edge+sink_y+sink_d/2)/2, z_top), counter)
add_box(island, "sink_bottom", (.57, .36, .015),
        (sink_x, sink_y, .915), (.37, .40, .38))
for i, x in enumerate([sink_x-.292, sink_x+.292]):
    add_box(island, "sink_side_%d" % i, (.015, .39, .073),
            (x, sink_y, .955), (.56, .59, .56))
for i, y in enumerate([sink_y-.187, sink_y+.187]):
    add_box(island, "sink_end_%d" % i, (.58, .015, .073),
            (sink_x, y, .955), (.56, .59, .56))
# Short economical faucet arch.
island.include("faucet", sweep_tube(
    points=[(.60,.40,1.005), (.60,.40,1.22),
            (.60,.36,1.27), (.60,.23,1.27), (.60,.20,1.22)],
    radius=.014, color=(.58,.62,.60)))
island.include("faucet_lever", rod(radius=.009,
    start=(.65,.40,1.025), end=(.65,.40,1.115),
    color=(.57,.60,.58)))
# Subtle rectangular hob outline on the left portion of the pale slab.
for i, y in enumerate([-.27, .12]):
    add_box(island, "hob_long_line_%d" % i, (.65,.008,.003),
            (-.56,y,1.010), (.49,.51,.47))
for i, x in enumerate([-.885,-.235]):
    add_box(island, "hob_short_line_%d" % i, (.008,.39,.003),
            (x,-.075,1.010), (.49,.51,.47))
scene.include("island", island)

hood = Asset("Large suspended ivory extractor")
add_box(hood, "rectangular_enclosure",
        (HOOD_WIDTH, HOOD_DEPTH, HOOD_TOP-HOOD_BOTTOM),
        (-.10, .32, (HOOD_TOP+HOOD_BOTTOM)/2), (.73,.72,.65))
add_box(hood, "bottom_plate", (1.10,.87,.022),
        (-.10,.32,HOOD_BOTTOM), (.55,.56,.51))
add_box(hood, "extractor_filter", (.73,.51,.008),
        (-.10,.32,HOOD_BOTTOM-.014), (.22,.25,.23))
scene.include("hood", hood)

kettle = Asset("Small red kettle")
kettle.include("body", ball(radius=.092, center=(-.52,1.82,1.035),
                            color=(.62,.006,.025)))
add_box(kettle, "base", (.16,.13,.025), (-.52,1.82,.955), black)
kettle.include("handle", sweep_tube(
    points=[(-.60,1.82,1.07),(-.60,1.82,1.16),
            (-.48,1.82,1.18),(-.43,1.82,1.10)],
    radius=.012, color=(.035,.025,.025)))
kettle.include("spout", rod(radius=.022,
    start=(-.45,1.81,1.05), end=(-.40,1.81,1.10),
    color=(.13,.14,.13)))
scene.include("kettle", kettle)

realize(scene)
set_view(CAMERA_POSITION, CAMERA_TARGET, lens=CAMERA_LENS)
camera = bpy.context.scene.camera
camera.data.sensor_fit = 'VERTICAL'
camera.data.sensor_height = 32

# Procedural timber grain and restrained material roughness.
for obj in bpy.context.scene.objects:
    if obj.type != 'MESH':
        continue
    for slot in obj.material_slots:
        mat = slot.material
        if mat is None:
            continue
        mat.use_nodes = True
        bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
        if bsdf:
            bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = .52
        if bsdf and "Base Color" in bsdf.inputs:
            c = bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value
            if c[0] > .30 and .15 < c[1] < .30 and c[2] < .18:
                nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes
                links = mat.node_tree.links
                tex = nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
                tex.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 4
                tex.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 3
                coords = nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
                mapping = nodes.new("ShaderNodeVectorMath")
                mapping.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
                mapping.inputs[1].default_value = (7,7,.28)
                links.new(coords.outputs["Generated"], mapping.inputs[0])
                links.new(mapping.outputs["Vector"], tex.inputs["Vector"])
                ramp = nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
                ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = .18
                ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (.17,.085,.035,1)
                ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = .82
                ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (.53,.34,.18,1)
                links.new(tex.outputs["Fac"], ramp.inputs[0])
                links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"], bsdf.inputs["Base Color"])

world = bpy.context.scene.world
if world is None:
    world = bpy.data.worlds.new("Kitchen world")
    bpy.context.scene.world = world
world.use_nodes = True
world.node_tree.nodes["Background"].inputs[0].default_value = (.28,.31,.32,1)
world.node_tree.nodes["Background"].inputs[1].default_value = .32

area_emitter((-2.3,-3.5,3.35), power=850, size=4.0,
             target=(0,.2,1.2), color=(1,.95,.86))
area_emitter((2.7,-.4,3.2), power=450, size=2.5,
             target=(0,0,1), color=(.89,.94,1))
area_emitter((-.65,1.78,1.43), power=38, size=1.7,
             target=(-.65,2.18,1.07), color=(1,.72,.50))
area_emitter((-2.5,1.0,3.25), power=160, size=1.5,
             target=(-1,1.8,1.1), color=(1,.93,.80))

# Source checks: all box dimensions are positive; rod endpoints and consecutive
# sweep points are distinct; repeated include keys carry indices. No fillet_box
# calls, external assets, render calls, save calls, or runner-setting changes.
```
